chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Jelly Roll's boasting, his ten-carat diamond and where his money came from
summary: Jelly Roll walked into joints buying the cat milk, claiming to be the greatest in the civilized world, and flashed a diamond later chiseled from his corpse.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Well, Jelly Roll could talk about all that, and people would be laughin'! Jelly Roll would walk in the joints, like...you know, and say, "Let's see the cat." Most joints have a cat around. "Give that cat a quart of milk." Just signifying. "Look at that mange. Get that dog a steak." Signify. Walk in, and people say, "A man come in town, Jelly Roll Morton. He bought the cat a quart of milk, he bought the dog a steak, and he's talkin' loud and he's playin' the piano, he say he's the greatest piano player in the Civilized World." He used that word, "Civilized world." [LAUGHS HEARTILY] You know, "I'm the greatest so-and-so in the Civilized world." And the people are...all them squares around the Rhythm Club lookin' at Jelly Roll. Then he opens his mouth; he got a diamond in his mouth. "Yeah, he's got a diamond." Wait til he open his jaws, make him mad so he can open his mouth. "What you say?!" And when you really looks, you see [LAUGHS] he got a big diamond -- about a 10-carat diamond.
Yeah, in them days he had all that stuff.
Some cat stole it when he went to California. He died, and the cat sneaked up ...(?)... one of these little hearses, took a chisel...
He raised his neck and chiseled that diamond out.
And sneaked that(?) undertaker for a (?).
Hey, Danny, is it true he had a dog, and he put it down there, and the dog... A bulldog? Somebody told me that he had a bulldog.
How'd he come by all that money in them days?
Oh, he was a Mack-Man. He had women. He had...
